method: Individual PDF review of pages 24–26; the arrest, possible supply, possible overdose and later allegations are distinguished rather than conflated.
words: the act of police taking someone into custody
An arrest stops a person's freedom of movement; learn make an arrest for the police action. Arrested does not mean convicted.
Police confirmed that an arrest had been made.
警方证实已经实施了一次逮捕。
Narrator says an arrest was logged but does not identify the exact offense or person.
a record listing reported criminal incidents
犯罪事件记录；治安事件日志
Log here means a written record, not wood. Pair crime with log to picture dated entries of reported incidents.
The campus website publishes a daily crime log.
校园网站发布每日治安事件记录。
A log records reports/incidents; it is not a list of convictions.
temporary, while waiting for a final decision or arrangement
Think of an interval between stages: interim fills the gap until a final arrangement. It does not mean permanent or final.
The team appointed an interim manager.
团队任命了一位临时经理。
Temporary measure pending investigation, not a final disciplinary outcome.
the authority to make decisions or apply rules in a particular area or matter
The juris- family connects with law, as in jurisprudence. Learn under the jurisdiction of + authority to remember who has power to decide.
The matter falls within the committee's jurisdiction.
这件事属于委员会的权限范围。
Narrator's assertion about campus authority, not a legal determination that location alone settles jurisdiction.
a drug used medically as an anesthetic and also used illicitly
涉及氯胺酮的违法事件
Say ketamine in three beats, KET-uh-meen. Treat it as a specific drug name, not a synonym for every anesthetic or illicit substance.
The report referred to a ketamine-related arrest.
报告提到了一次与氯胺酮有关的逮捕。
Reported substance name only; no dosage, use instructions or determination of the exact offense.
took an amount of a drug greater than the body could safely tolerate
over- means too much; dose is an amount. Overdose adds d to become overdosed, with final /st/ rather than a new syllable.
The report alleged that someone had overdosed.
报告称有人药物摄入过量。
Source calls this an allegation and says the relation to the arrest is unknown; do not merge identities or establish a diagnosis.
the state of having or controlling something
possess becomes possession; keep the double s in both places. Possession means having/control, not necessarily legal ownership.
She was in possession of the original document.
Having the substance is distinct from supplying it; source presents alternatives, not a settled account.
courteous, honorable, and considerate in a traditional ideal of conduct
有骑士风度的；礼貌而重荣誉的
Connect chivalrous with chivalry, the knightly ideal. Initial ch is /ʃ/, unlike chair; picture an old-fashioned courtesy.
The story describes a chivalrous gesture.
故事描述了一个有骑士风度的举动。
Quoted ideal in a creed; no judgment that the organization lived up to it.
a statement of beliefs or principles held by a group or person
The long ee in creed sounds /i/. Picture a short written set of beliefs; distinguish creed from greed, desire for more.
该团体的信条强调诚实。
Institutional belief statement, not a legal code or a proven description of conduct.
a person's honesty and consistency with moral principles
Integrity can mean wholeness; personal integrity connects actions and principles into a consistent whole. Remember acting honestly even when unobserved.
Her colleagues respected her personal integrity.
同事们尊重她的个人操守。
Stated founding ideal, not a factual certification of any member's character.
special permissions or benefits available to a person or group
Privilege ends in /dʒ/, so privileges adds /ɪz/. Here permissions can be withdrawn; do not equate every privilege with a universal right.
Members can lose their booking privileges.
成员可能会失去预约权限。
Party-hosting permissions in imagined institutional response; not a confirmed sanction in that sentence.
a name used instead of a person's real name
pseudo- means false or assumed and -onym relates to name. Initial p is silent: SOO-duh-nim.
The author published the article under a pseudonym.
作者以化名发表了这篇文章。
Jane Doe is identified as an assumed name; no attempt to identify the person behind it.
a second-year student in a US high school or university
Learn the sequence freshman → sophomore → junior → senior. Attach sophomore to year two instead of guessing age from the word.
She changed her major during her sophomore year.
Academic year, not a guarantee of exactly two completed years; the narrator's timeline remains attributed.
a group connected by a place, institution, or shared interests
Common and community suggest something shared. Here the shared connection is campus life, not necessarily one residential neighborhood.
The event brought the campus community together.
这场活动把校园里的师生群体聚到了一起。
Campus social group, not an online-platform feature or a geographic town alone.
encouraging interest in or support for something
promote drops final e before -ing. Promoting an activity increases interest; promoting an employee gives a higher job, a different sense.
The club is promoting its new activities.
这个社团正在宣传新活动。
Encouraging Greek-life participation as reported by the speaker, not promoting someone to a higher position.
a temporary stopping of participation, activity, or permission
暂停一个团体的活动资格
Suspend becomes suspension, with /ʃ/ in -sion. Picture an activity paused while a decision is pending, not permanently ended.
The club was placed on temporary suspension.
该社团被暂时停止活动。
Organizational activity status, not necessarily suspension of each student's studies.
providing something that another person needs or receives
Supply keeps y before -ing: supplying. Follow supplying with the thing provided, then to the recipient if needed.
The company is supplying equipment to local schools.
这家公司正在向本地学校供应设备。
Supply of a substance is only speculated about in the source; not established as the arrest charge.
honesty and adherence to consistent moral principles
Connect integrity with being whole: principles and actions fit together. In this passage it is moral integrity, not data/file integrity.
We expect everyone to act with integrity.
我们希望每个人都以诚信行事。
Moral principle listed in the creed; not certification of actual behavior.
to build relationships that may offer social or professional opportunities
A net links points; network as a verb links people. Here you network, rather than connect a computer to a network.
The event gives students a chance to network with alumni.
这场活动给学生提供了与校友建立联系的机会。
Verb about relationships, not a computer system or television network.
to examine information carefully to find out what happened
Connect investigate with investigation: drop final e and add -ion for the noun. Investigating gathers facts; it does not itself prove guilt.
The university said it would investigate the complaint.
大学表示将调查这起投诉。
Imagined institutional response introduced by the narrator; not an actual announcement newly verified here.
phrases: to be exact
used to make a previous statement more precise
确切地说
We waited an hour—sixty-five minutes, to be exact.
我们等了一个小时，确切地说是六十五分钟。
Specifies which house, not proof of the precise offense.
word is his bond
a person's promise can be trusted as a binding commitment
言出必行；一诺千金
He believes his word is his bond and keeps his promises.
他相信应当一诺千金，并信守承诺。
Fixed proverb; bond means binding promise, not a financial security. Source uses a traditional masculine formulation.
falls apart
stops functioning or collapses, literally or figuratively
崩溃；瓦解
The plan falls apart if nobody confirms the booking.
如果没人确认预订，计划就会泡汤。
Figurative disruption of the person's situation; does not mean literal bodily disintegration.
made national news
received news coverage across the country
成为全国性新闻
The discovery made national news.
这一发现成为了全国性新闻。
Source says never made national news at that stage; preserve negation.
kicking people out
forcing people to leave a place or group
把人赶出去；逐出
The manager said they were not kicking people out.
经理说，他们并没有要把人赶出去。
Not literally kicking; source imagined response distinguishes investigation from eviction.
segments: Date fragment introduces the repeated full date in 377; no audio time inferred.
Sets date and location with kind of as a hedge; busy day is an ordinary phrase anticipating several events.
Drug-related arrest and exact house stated; exact charge is not established and must not be inferred from the substance alone.
Does not place on interim suspension is negative; because they're going to host another party is the narrator's reasoning and does not become an official policy explanation.
Ketamine-related offense remains nonspecific; inconsistent Kai-Fai spelling is preserved as printed.
Explicit statement that the precise offense is unknown; essential uncertainty carried forward.
Snippets and get into in a second need support; Title IX is a named investigation framework requiring context, not a label for a criminal conviction. Overdose remains an allegation.
Do know contrasts with unknown offense; logged means recorded. Cornell fragment is corrected by a new clause in 384.
Daily crime log is a record of reports/incidents, not a record proving guilt.
Maybe and unfinished or explicitly mark speculation; do not label the arrestee a supplier as fact.
Repeated if clauses enumerate alternatives; supply, possession and overdose are distinct, and the number/identity of individuals is unknown.
Some sort of and related retain nonspecificity; location/date repeated without adding an offense.
On campus locates the building and leads into a jurisdiction claim, not independent verification of ownership.
Negated off campus contrasts location; technically and right frame the speaker's asserted inference about authority, not legal advice.
Incomplete do nothing to leads directly into give suspension in 391; no missing object invented.
Temporary suspension is what others reportedly expected, not what is reported to have happened.
Not supposed to means prohibited/against expectations, not inability; fixed expression deserves explicit learner support.
Imagined institutional speech continues 392; not a newly verified first-person police quote.
Shut down means stop operations; still imagined response, not the actual action at that moment.
Ragers and keg stands remain cultural/slang gaps; profanity intensifies partying. Imagined sanction distinguishes lost event privileges from eviction.
Rhetorical confirmation request about the expected response, not a universal institutional rule.
But they don't negates the expected response and returns to the narrated account.
Alleges explicitly frames the assault claim; sophomore is second-year student. Duration and age are quoted, not independently verified.
Touts itself and motto are useful vocabulary gaps; building better men is a quoted slogan contrasted with allegations, not endorsed by the lesson.
Founding principles are professed ideals; truth/honor/integrity are not a finding about actual conduct.
Whether...or and hand of brotherhood is extended are rhetorical patterns still needing support; literal hand extension alone misses welcoming assistance metaphor.
Declaration of belief within the creed, not narration certifying the group's behavior.
Foundations upon which is a formal relative construction: principles are the metaphorical basis, not actual building foundations.
Proverb means keeping promises; no financial-bond or physical-word interpretation.
Crosses the ages and touch the heart are figurative rhetoric; chivalrous alone does not resolve the whole line.
Jane Doe explicitly an assumed name; her starting at Cornell means enrollment/beginning studies. Details are from her civil pleading, not a judgment.
Lawsuit dropped here likely means released/filed, unlike drop a lawsuit meaning withdraw it. Needs a context-specific explanation before closure.
Distinguishes incident year from later public discussion; informal big conversation means extensive discussion, not one physical meeting.
National coverage phrase now explicit, but Title IX investigation still needs a sourced institutional-framework note; not a synonym for police prosecution.
Abandoned relative clause after that; next paragraph starts a contrast. Preserve the fragment.
Unless = except if; repeated conditions limit who knew about the situation. What was going on means what was happening, not physical movement.
Not just...but and repeated as well as enumerate defendants; a lawsuit against them does not establish liability.
Get into means discuss in detail, not physically enter; promises later explanation.
Case breaks open means becomes exposed/develops publicly in context, not a physical container opening or a final judicial resolution.
Completes relevant details of her starting at Cornell from 414; not a standalone new event.
Falls apart is figurative deterioration of her situation; academic year named rather than a precise elapsed duration.
About marks approximation; do not reconcile it into an exact enrollment date from sophomore alone.
Tri Delta is explicitly expanded as three Deltas; named group and reported motivation, not a new general vocabulary sense.
Short acknowledgment with no independent learning barrier.
Kept promoting means repeatedly encouraged; vital means very important, and she felt like attributes the perceived message to her experience.
Network is build relationships; made it seem like and seems frame an impression of safety, not proof that the environment was safe.
Abrupt joins Tri Delta October 19th wording may fuse prior enrollment with the incident date. Preserve the transcript but do not assert a verified joining date without audio/context confirmation.
